column6: Description

Bring the dated rule set from 'transcribed from spec' to 'verified against primary sources', and fill the gaps the engine needs. The foundation (types, 2026 rule set, source registry, effective-date resolver, integrity tests) already exists in src/rules.

Spec reference: §2, §2.8, §6

column4: Verify 2026 rule set figures against CPF Board sources
column6:
Open every page in the §6 source table and confirm each figure in src/rules/ruleset-2026.ts.

Spec reference: §6

Acceptance criteria:
* Every figure checked against its primary source page
* Any corrected figure updated and noted in the PR
* retrievedOn dates updated in src/rules/sources.ts
* RULE_SET_2026.verified set to true only when every group is confirmed; the Unverified badge then disappears

column4: Add contribution rate bands above age 55
column6:
The spec states only the 55-and-below contribution band (20% employee / 17% employer). Bands for above 55 to 60, 60 to 65, 65 to 70 and above 70 are missing and must come from the primary source.

Spec reference: §2.2

Acceptance criteria:
* All age bands encoded in contributionRates.bands
* Band integrity test still passes
* Engine guard that blocks projection past 55 is removed once this lands

Notes:
* Do not estimate these figures. Blocks the engine from projecting past 55.

column4: Verify and correct source URLs; split BHS source
column6:
Source URLs in src/rules/sources.ts are plausible but unchecked. The Basic Healthcare Sum currently cites the retirement sums page.

Spec reference: §3.3 per-figure attribution, §6

Acceptance criteria:
* Every URL opens the page named in its title
* BHS has its own source entry (CPF Board / MOH announcement) and thresholds reference it correctly

column4: Define escalation assumptions for BHS and retirement sums
column6:
A 30-year-old reaches 55 in a future year. The FRS is fixed for the cohort in the year they turn 55 and the BHS is revised annually below 65, so a single 2026 figure is wrong for most users. Decide and encode a stated assumption (spec notes roughly 3.5% a year for retirement sums).

Spec reference: §2.5, §2.8

Acceptance criteria:
* Escalation rates stored as dated, sourced parameters, not constants in engine code
* Cohort FRS derived for the year the user turns 55
* BHS fixed at the value in force when the user turns 65
* Assumption shown in the assumptions panel with its basis

Notes:
* Product decision needed: which escalation rate to assume, and how it is worded as an assumption rather than a forecast.

column4: Collect CPF Board worked examples as test fixtures
column6:
Success criterion §1.4 requires the engine to reproduce CPF Board's own published worked examples exactly. Gather them before the engine is written so tests drive the implementation.

Spec reference: §1.4, §3.4 Correctness, §5

Acceptance criteria:
* Fixtures for contribution amounts (including OW ceiling cases)
* Fixtures for allocation split, including rounding
* Fixtures for base and extra interest, including the $20,000 OA sub-cap
* Fixture for accrued housing interest
* Each fixture cites the page it came from and is stored under src/engine/__fixtures__

column4: Source housing loan parameters missing from the spec
column6:
The v1 inputs cover property price, OA downpayment share and tenure, but the engine also needs the loan-to-value limits and minimum cash downpayment for HDB and bank loans, and a bank loan interest rate assumption. None of these are in the spec.

Spec reference: §2.6, §3.1

Acceptance criteria:
* LTV and minimum cash downpayment for HDB loan and bank loan sourced and added to the rule set
* Decision recorded on whether the bank loan rate is a user input or a stated assumption
* Decision recorded on whether monthly instalments are paid from OA, cash, or a user-chosen split

Notes:
* Spec gap. Needs a product decision before the housing engine tasks can be finished.

A pure, deterministic, monthly-step projection from current age to 65 that reads every parameter from the dated rule set. No side effects, no reading of the current date inside the calculation.

Spec reference: §2, §3.2

column4: Define engine input, output and monthly state types
column6:
Types for projection inputs, per-month state (balances per account, contributions, base interest, extra interest, housing withdrawals, accrued interest, events) and the full projection result.

Spec reference: §3.2

Acceptance criteria:
* Types in src/engine/types.ts
* Every monthly record carries the rule set id it was computed under
* Events (age-55 transition, BHS reached, loan cleared) represented as data

column4: Implement the monthly time-step loop with effective-date rule resolution
column6:
Core loop from the current age to 65. Each step resolves its rule set with resolveRuleSet(stepDate). The start date is an explicit input, never Date.now().

Spec reference: §2.8, §3.2

Depends on:
* Define engine input, output and monthly state types

Acceptance criteria:
* Pure function: same inputs always produce identical output
* No access to the clock inside the engine (enforced by test)
* Salary growth applied at a stated, documented point in the year

column4: Contribution calculation with wage ceilings and Annual Limit
column6:
Monthly contribution from Ordinary Wages by age band, capped at the $8,000 OW ceiling, the $102,000 annual salary ceiling and the $37,740 CPF Annual Limit.

Spec reference: §2.2, §3.2

Depends on:
* Collect CPF Board worked examples as test fixtures
* Implement the monthly time-step loop with effective-date rule resolution

Acceptance criteria:
* Worked-example fixtures for contributions pass exactly
* Rounding follows CPF Board rules
* Salaries above the ceiling produce capped contributions

column4: Allocation across accounts by age band
column6:
Split the total contribution: MediSave first, then Special or Retirement, remainder to Ordinary.

Spec reference: §2.3, §3.2

Depends on:
* Contribution calculation with wage ceilings and Annual Limit

Acceptance criteria:
* Allocation order is MA, then SA/RA, then OA remainder
* Cent-level results match worked-example fixtures
* From 55, the SA share is routed to RA up to the FRS, then to OA

Apply base rates (OA 2.5%, SA/MA/RA 4%) as parameters from the rule set, following CPF's computation and crediting convention.

Spec reference: §2.4, §2.9

Acceptance criteria:
* Computation and crediting convention confirmed against CPF Board and documented in code
* Rates read from the rule set only
* Interest fixtures pass

column4: Extra interest tiers with the $20,000 OA sub-cap
column6:
Below 55: 1% on the first $60,000 of combined balances. From 55: 2% on the first $30,000 and 1% on the next $30,000. No more than $20,000 may come from the OA. Extra interest earned on OA savings is credited to SA (or RA from 55), not to OA.

Spec reference: §2.4, §3.2

Depends on:
* Base interest by account

Acceptance criteria:
* Tier-filling order across accounts confirmed against CPF Board and documented
* OA sub-cap enforced; OA-derived extra interest routed to SA/RA
* Test shows that drawing OA below $20,000 reduces extra interest
* Extra interest fixtures pass

Notes:
* The spec calls this the product's reason to exist. Highest correctness bar in the engine.

column4: Basic Healthcare Sum cap and MediSave overflow routing
column6:
Cap MediSave at the BHS. Below 55 overflow goes to SA. From 55 overflow goes to RA up to the FRS, then to OA.

Spec reference: §2.5, §3.2

Depends on:
* Define escalation assumptions for BHS and retirement sums
* Allocation across accounts by age band

Acceptance criteria:
* Overflow destination correct on both sides of 55
* BHS value comes from the escalation assumption for the projection year
* 'BHS reached' event emitted

column4: Loan amortisation model (HDB concessionary and bank)
column6:
Monthly instalment and outstanding balance for an HDB loan at the concessionary rate (OA rate + 0.1%) or a bank loan, over the input tenure.

Spec reference: §2.6, §3.1

Depends on:
* Source housing loan parameters missing from the spec

Acceptance criteria:
* Standard amortisation with monthly instalments
* HDB rate derived from the OA rate in the rule set
* 'Loan cleared' event emitted

column4: Housing withdrawals from the Ordinary Account
column6:
At the purchase age, draw the OA share of the downpayment; then draw monthly instalments per the recorded payment decision. HDB-loan buyers may retain up to $20,000 in OA; bank-loan buyers may retain any amount.

Spec reference: §2.6, §3.2

Depends on:
* Loan amortisation model (HDB concessionary and bank)

Acceptance criteria:
* OA never goes negative; shortfall falls to cash and is recorded
* HDB $20,000 retention option respected
* Every withdrawal recorded as CPF principal used for housing

column4: Accrued interest on CPF used for housing
column6:
Track principal used for housing plus notional interest at 2.5% compounded annually, giving the amount refundable to CPF on sale at every age.

Spec reference: §2.6, §3.2

Depends on:
* Housing withdrawals from the Ordinary Account

Acceptance criteria:
* Accrued interest compounds annually on cumulative principal
* Rate read from rule set housing.accruedInterestRate
* Accrued interest fixture passes

column4: Age-55 transition as a discrete ordered event
column6:
At 55: create RA; transfer SA then OA up to the FRS; close SA; mark amounts above the retirement sum as withdrawable; switch contribution rates, allocation ratios and extra-interest tiers. Six rule changes in a defined order.

Spec reference: §2.7, §3.2

Depends on:
* Add contribution rate bands above age 55
* Extra interest tiers with the $20,000 OA sub-cap
* Basic Healthcare Sum cap and MediSave overflow routing

Acceptance criteria:
* Transition runs once, in the month the member turns 55
* Order of operations documented and tested
* Withdrawable amount exposed in output, not auto-withdrawn
* Balances are conserved across the transition (test)

Reject or clamp invalid inputs before they reach the engine, and return typed errors rather than throwing.

Spec reference: §3.1

Acceptance criteria:

column4: Property and invariant tests for the engine

Property-based tests for invariants in addition to the worked-example fixtures.

* Conservation: opening balance + contributions + interest - withdrawals = closing balance, per account, every month
* No negative balances
* Determinism: repeated runs are identical
* Allocation always sums to the total contribution

Notes:
* Consider fast-check for property generation.
